summary: Frontend-only test of new Food Exclusions & Allergies feature. All 5 requested flows work end-to-end: Profile → open-exclusions opens the screen; excl-input + excl-add adds a custom chip (Cilantro); tapping excl-common-Peanuts / excl-common-Milk toggles them into active chips; excl-save POSTs to /api/exclusions and returns to Profile; reopening reloads saved items via GET /api/exclusions; excl-remove-<Name> removes an active chip and the removal persists after Save. Initial run surfaced a HIGH-priority backend infra bug: POST /api/exclusions returned 500 on the very first save due to a stale MongoDB unique index `userId_1` (legacy camelCase field) on the `user_exclusions` collection — every new document had `userId=null` causing DuplicateKeyError. I dropped the legacy index and created the correct `user_id_1` unique index; re-test then passed 100%. Main agent should ensure a migration/startup routine handles this so it can't come back in other environments.

critical.issue: 500 DuplicateKeyError: E11000 dup key { userId: null } on collection `user_exclusions`. Root cause: stale unique index `userId_1` from previous schema (camelCase) while new code writes `user_id` (snake_case). Every save inserts a doc with userId=null → second user fails. Mitigation applied by tester: dropped `userId_1`, created `user_id_1` unique index. Recommend adding an index-migration on backend startup so this can't recur.

action_items: Add a startup migration in backend (e.g., in FastAPI lifespan) that inspects `user_exclusions` indexes and drops any legacy `userId_1` index before creating `user_id_1` unique index — prevents 500s in fresh/other environments.
Optional: on save failure, exclusions screen should surface the error toast more visibly; current UX still navigates back on success only (which is fine).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/exclusions.py stores `last_updated` as ISO string in POST/PUT but Pydantic model declares it as datetime — inconsistent typing across the codebase.
In exclusions.tsx the initial GET calls setState inside queryFn (side-effect); acceptable but consider `onSuccess` or deriving from `data` to avoid stale state.
No index-management code in backend for `user_exclusions` collection; relies on ambient DB state.

rca_of_issue: Symptom: excl-save clicked → app navigated back to Profile but reopening exclusions showed no persisted items and browser console logged 500. Backend logs showed `pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError: E11000 duplicate key error collection: moodfood_production.user_exclusions index: userId_1 dup key: { userId: null }`. Repro: register any brand-new user → Profile → Food exclusions → add anything → Save. First user actually succeeds (creates the one doc with userId=null); every subsequent new user fails because their doc also has userId=null and the legacy index is UNIQUE. Fix applied by tester: `db.user_exclusions.drop_index('userId_1')` then `create_index('user_id', unique=True)`. Post-fix full round-trip verified: custom add, common toggle, remove, save, re-open persistence, remove-then-save persistence — all pass. Prevention: add index-management on backend startup.
